title: Two Men Died Over a Roll of Duct Tape
tested_variable: baseline (first video - nothing to compare against yet)

source.publisher: U.S. Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board (CSB)
source.title: Case Study: Confined Space Entry - Worker and Would-be Rescuer Asphyxiated. Valero Energy Corporation Refinery, Delaware City, DE, November 5, 2005

beats.narration: Two men died over this roll of duct tape.

claims.claim: Two workers died.
claims.quote: asphyxiation death of two contractor employees

claims.claim: The first was trying to get a roll of tape out of the vessel.
claims.quote: in an attempt to retrieve a roll of tape from inside the vessel, was overcome by nitrogen, collapsed in the vessel, and died

claims.claim: The second died trying to rescue him.
claims.quote: was asphyxiated while attempting to rescue him

claims.claim: It was a roll of duct tape.
claims.quote: a roll of duct tape was lying on the

beats.narration: And what killed them, you're breathing right now.

claims.claim: They died of nitrogen asphyxiation.
claims.quote: nitrogen asphyxiation death of two

claims.claim: Nitrogen is 78 percent of the air we breathe.
claims.quote: Nitrogen, which makes up 78 percent of the air we breathe, is non-toxic

beats.narration: Night shift at a Delaware refinery. A crew has to reinstall a pipe on top of this reactor.

claims.claim: Date of the incident.
claims.quote: November 5, 2005, nitrogen asphyxiation death of two

claims.claim: It happened at a refinery in Delaware City, Delaware.
claims.quote: refinery in Delaware City, Delaware

claims.claim: It was a night-shift crew.
claims.quote: Matrix nightshift boilermaker crew

claims.claim: They were preparing to reassemble a pipe on the vessel.
claims.quote: preparing to reassemble a pipe on a pressure vessel

claims.claim: The job was to install the top elbow.
claims.quote: top elbow

claims.claim: The vessel was the hydrocracker reactor, R1.
claims.quote: reactor (R1)

claims.claim: The work included reinstalling the stud nuts (bolting).
claims.quote: reinstalling the stud nuts and washers

claims.claim: The pipe goes on the reactor's top manway.
claims.quote: Pipe assembly connects 12-inch diameter process pipe to the reactor top manway

claims.claim: Reconstruction geometry: the manway opening is 24 inches (other dimensions from Figures 6 and 7, which are images).
claims.quote: Because the manway opening was only 24 inches

beats.narration: Someone spots a roll of duct tape, five feet down inside. It can't stay there.

claims.claim: A pipefitter pointed out the roll of duct tape.
claims.quote: a Matrix pipefitter told them that a roll of duct tape was lying on the

claims.claim: It was about five feet below the opening.
claims.quote: about five feet below the opening

claims.claim: Cleanliness criteria meant it could not be left inside.
claims.quote: reactor cleanliness criteria prohibited leaving the tape inside the reactor

beats.narration: Going in means a permit and a delay. So they make a wire hook.

claims.claim: Entry would need a trained crew and an entry permit.
claims.quote: knew entry would require a specially trained and equipped crew and confined space

claims.claim: That would delay the work.
claims.quote: which would delay their work, possibly beyond the end of their work shift

claims.claim: They decided to make a long wire hook instead.
claims.quote: they decided to make a long wire hook

claims.claim: The wire was fifteen feet long.
claims.quote: Fifteen foot wire with hook formed on end

beats.narration: But their permit left one thing out: the reactor is full of nitrogen. No warning sign. No barricade.

claims.claim: The boilermakers' permit did not tell them about the nitrogen purge.
claims.quote: safe work permit did not inform them that the reactor was on nitrogen purge

claims.claim: The nitrogen purge status on the permit was marked N/A.
claims.quote: the nitrogen purge status was marked "N/A" on the permit even though the reactor continued to be purged with nitrogen

claims.claim: The reactor was nitrogen-filled.
claims.quote: Nobody saw him enter the nitrogen-filled reactor

claims.claim: No nitrogen warning sign or barricade was in place.
claims.quote: a nitrogen purge warning sign and barricade were not in place in the work area

claims.claim: Nitrogen was venting out through the manway.
claims.quote: The nitrogen purge gas was slowly venting out of the reactor through the manway

claims.claim: The permit form has a 'nitrogen purge or inerted' Yes/No/NA box.
claims.quote: "nitrogen purge or inerted" (Yes/No/NA) status

claims.claim: Procedure required a barricade and warning signs before the purge started.
claims.quote: The procedures required operators to install a barricade and post warning signs at all equipment access points

claims.claim: The permit was to install the top elbow.
claims.quote: top elbow

claims.claim: Red danger tape on the studs was the only warning on the manway (shown, not narrated).
claims.quote: the red tape was the only warning on the manway

claims.claim: The purge vented straight onto the work platform (shown as the plume over the manway, not narrated).
claims.quote: the reactor was on a nitrogen purge that vented directly onto the work platform area

beats.narration: No smell. No color. Almost no oxygen.

claims.claim: Nitrogen is odorless and colorless.
claims.quote: nitrogen, which is odorless, tasteless, and colorless

claims.claim: Oxygen inside the reactor was near zero.
claims.quote: the oxygen concentration was near zero

claims.claim: Normal air is about 21 percent oxygen.
claims.quote: The normal oxygen concentration in air is about 21 percent

claims.claim: 19.5 percent is the minimum safe level.
claims.quote: 19.5 Minimum safe level

beats.narration: The first man tries standing. Then kneeling.

claims.claim: He tried standing, then kneeling.
claims.quote: He tried from a standing position next to the manway and then, apparently to get closer, tried kneeling on the platform next to the manway

claims.claim: CSB concluded he likely sat on the narrow ledge.
claims.quote: the CSB concluded that the first victim likely stepped over the manway studs and then sat on the narrow ledge

claims.claim: The ledge between the studs and the opening.
claims.quote: The first victim most likely sat on the narrow reactor manway ledge between the studs and the opening to get closer to the tape

claims.claim: Nobody saw him enter; whether he fell or went in on purpose is unknown.
claims.quote: Nobody saw him enter the nitrogen-filled reactor, but he either fell in or intentionally went into the reactor

beats.narration: In that air, one or two breaths and you're down.

claims.claim: Collapse comes within one or two breaths.
claims.quote: he would collapse from a lack of oxygen within one or two breaths

claims.claim: Loss of consciousness follows after only one or two breaths.
claims.quote: After only one or two breaths the oxygen concentration in the blood drops dangerously low

claims.claim: The first man was found on the tray, five feet below the manway (shown, not narrated).
claims.quote: saw two victims lying motionless inside the reactor on the tray five feet below the manway

beats.narration: His foreman grabs a ladder and climbs in to save him. A few breaths later, he's down too.

claims.claim: The foreman grabbed a ladder and climbed into the reactor.
claims.quote: the foreman grabbed a nearby ladder, shoved it down the manway, and quickly climbed in the reactor

claims.claim: He was trying to rescue his co-worker.
claims.quote: His co-worker, the crew foreman, was asphyxiated while attempting to rescue him

claims.claim: He succumbed within a few breaths.
claims.quote: Within a few breaths the foreman was the second victim to succumb to oxygen deprivation

claims.claim: The foreman and the contract administrator looked through the manway first (shown, not narrated).
claims.quote: saw the boilermaker foreman (the second victim) and the nightshift contract administrator looking through the manway into R1

beats.narration: A third man reaches the ladder. He stops, and radios for help.

claims.claim: The contract administrator approached the ladder, hesitated, and radioed for help.
claims.quote: saw the nightshift contract administrator approach the ladder, hesitate, and then heard him urgently call for help on his radio

claims.claim: Staying out and radioing was the trained response that would have kept the foreman alive.
claims.quote: he would have immediately announced the emergency on the radio and remained on the platform, safely away from the manway until qualified emergency response personnel arrived

beats.narration: Responders arrive in under two minutes.

claims.claim: Emergency responders reached the platform in less than two minutes.
claims.quote: arrived on the platform in less than two minutes

claims.claim: Responders wore breathing apparatus (shown, not narrated).
claims.quote: A Valero operator put on his self-contained breathing air respirator then entered the reactor

beats.narration: Never follow someone into a tank. Call it in.
onscreen: OF CONFINED-SPACE DEATHS IN ONE STUDY

claims.claim: Only trained, equipped personnel should attempt a rescue.
claims.quote: Only qualified and trained personnel equipped with the necessary safety equipment should attempt a rescue

claims.claim: In one study 39 percent of confined-space deaths were would-be rescuers.
claims.quote: of 88 total confined space entry fatalities, 34 workers (39 percent) died while attempting to rescue a co-worker

beats.narration: Two men never came home. We tell their story so no other family goes through this.
onscreen: A worker with nearly 10 years in refineries.
One died trying to save the other.

claims.claim: Both men died.
claims.quote: transported to the hospital where they were pronounced dead

claims.claim: Two died; the second was attempting a rescue.
claims.quote: asphyxiation death of two contractor employees

claims.claim: The foreman died attempting to rescue the first worker.
claims.quote: was asphyxiated while attempting to rescue him

claims.claim: Their experience.
claims.quote: The first victim had nearly ten years experience working in refineries; the second had more than 25

claims.claim: Date and place.
claims.quote: November 5, 2005, nitrogen asphyxiation death of two
